description:
Inspect Objective

Read one objective's planning state: setup, audience, forecast, and sourcing. Read-only.

These actions write no records. Every action takes id = objective UUID.
- objective_pilot_review: read expired-pilot evidence, owner, next check,
  and decision/preparation history (latest 20 entries; has_more marks the bound).
- objective_business: read business intent, contribution links and owned work;
  task and child completion never substitute for this objective's result.
- objective_setup_context: read the Architect inputs.
- objective_setup_list: read saved setup reviews, optionally filtered by
  payload {action_id}.
- objective_audience: read paginated accounts or people (payload =
  {view: "accounts"|"people", query?, status?, company_id?, unresolved?,
  limit?, offset?}). Counts and account outreach are projections.
- objective_audience_build: read the deterministic audience volume plan,
  required research facts, and latest saved sourcing run (optional payload
  = {pilot_size: 1-100}). Does not attach CRM people, invoke a model, or
  start providers. A pilot is not a meeting forecast. Includes
  brief_context_fingerprint and research_brief_stale for reviewed briefs.
  fact_definitions lists workspace definitions with description,
  subject_type, and answer_schema. For an equivalent public question, copy
  these as fact_definition, subject_type and answer_schema in the reviewed
  brief. Leave fact_definition unset for private conversations and
  interpretations.
- objective_forecast: read the current derived path distribution, weekly
  channel load, target math, five sample plans, commitments, abstentions,
  and prior-forecast diff (no payload). blocking_reasons must be resolved
  before manage_outreach action=objective_launch.
  pilot_sequence_claim_required means the reviewed sequence and rationale
  are not yet saved through manage_outreach action=objective_pin.
- objective_sourcing_plan: calculate the exact cohort size, live provider
  order, bounded cost and candidate limits, and blocking reasons. Optional
  payload {pilot_size: 1-100} requests an explicit pilot audience size
  including existing eligible members, without an assumed or observed
  conversion rate. Each call runs Vruum's sourcing planner model within
  the workspace's model budget; over budget, the plan returns without
  the planner's advice.
- objective_sourcing_run: read saved preparation counts and recovery
  (payload = {action_id}).
- objective_sourcing_recovery: read saved failure phase, resume
  eligibility, and current reviewed_inputs (payload = {job_id}).
  manage_outreach action=objective_sourcing_resume takes those
  reviewed_inputs.

### Responses:

**200**: Successful Response (Success Response)
Content-Type: application/json

Objective audience preparation support (objective_sourcing):
Product support is not permission. Inspect current work and follow the domain's authorization and review rules.
- plan: inspect_objective action=objective_sourcing_plan. Read the current cohort plan and provider envelope; no new discovery.
- propose: manage_outreach action=objective_source. Prepare sourcing review; existing matching records may be attached before paid discovery.
- approve: manage_outreach action=objective_source_approve. Approve the exact current sourcing plan under domain policy; no launch or message approval.
- inspect: inspect_objective action=objective_sourcing_run. Read saved counts and recovery state by Action; queued or completed work is not a revenue outcome.
- stop: manage_outreach action=objective_sourcing_stop. Stop further work using the expected Action version; an in-flight request may still finish.
- recovery_review: inspect_objective action=objective_sourcing_recovery. Read current inputs and whether this saved job can resume.
- resume: manage_outreach action=objective_sourcing_resume. Explicitly approve recovery with reviewed inputs; preserve saved work and block uncertain provider effects.
- provider_receipt: unsupported. Saved preparation counts do not expose authoritative provider receipts.
- reconcile_provider_effect: unsupported. An operator must investigate uncertain provider effects; do not retry discovery blindly.
- unattended_continuation: unsupported. Terminal failures need explicit recovery review; existing bounded retries are not general copilot continuation.
- executor_transfer: unsupported. No accepted preparation handoff between a harness and a worker exists.
- business_outcome_measurement: unsupported. Sourcing counts do not establish replies, opportunities, or revenue.

action.description: The operation to perform — see the tool description for the action vocabulary and each action's id/payload semantics.
action.title: action

for_company.description: Optional company ID or name (UUID, or case-insensitive EXACT name match — partial / substring matches are NOT supported; ambiguous names raise 400) to execute this tool as. Use get_operator_companies, or get_operator_overview with view='companies', to list available companies. Only needed if you manage multiple companies. Access is enforced server-side: the tool resolves the value to a user_company_id and verifies the caller's membership in `company_users` — a 403 'Company not found or access denied' means EITHER the value did not match a known company OR the caller is not a member of it. The MCP operator role itself is NOT auto-granted — operators get this access by being members of each client company via `company_users` (the same row that grants any normal user access).
for_company.title: for_company

id.description: Target entity id, or an ARRAY of ids to apply the same action+payload to each (max 100; see the tool description for which entity the id names per action).
id.title: id

items.description: For create-like actions only: an array of per-item payloads processed in order with per-item results (max 100). Mutually exclusive with `id` and `payload`.
items.title: items

payload.description: Action-specific fields, validated by the underlying route's own schema (a bad field 422s with that route's precise errors). See the tool description per action.
payload.title: payload
